newsitem.title: USA: Physician Sales sees Q4 loss on higher revs.
newsitem.headline: Physician Sales sees Q4 loss on higher revs.

text.p: Physician Sales & Service Inc Monday said it expects to post a fourth quarter loss due to acquisition-related charges despite higher revenues.
The company sees a loss per share of $0.05 to $0.07 for the fourth quarter ended March 28 compared to $0.12 a share last year. It will releases earnings on May 27.

The loss per share will include several acquisition related charges which come to a total of $0.19 to $0.24 a share. The acquisition of imaging and x-ray distributors will account for $0.10 to $0.12 of costs and expenses; expenses for charges for unrealized acquisition related assets of $0.07 to $0.09 for core business mergers; and lower-than expected operating results of recently acquired core business mergers in transition of $0.02 to $0.03.

The distributor of medical supplies and equipment recently bought several diagnostic imaging and x-ray distributors. To improve gross margins, it cut over $25 million of low margin annualized revenues over the past two quarters and in a statement, said it sees "positive results and trends in its gross margins" from the action.
It said fourth quarter revenues should rise 30 percent to about $187 million from last year. For the year, revenues should also increase 30 percent to $690 million.

Chairman and chief executive Patrick Kelly said in the statement, "While the anticipated earnings decline was unexpected, our review of these results indicate that they are one time in nature and we believe that they are non- recurring. For our most recent acquisitions we have changed our method of reserving and escrowing for the realization of assets acquired."
Shares closed on Friday on the Nasdaq at 14.
